articleTitle: Performance and Wake Recovery Analysis of A Lift-driven Helical Hydrokinetic Turbine: A Numerical Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The lift-driven helical hydrokinetic turbine (LHHT) technology is one of the promising options to facilitate a green source of renewable power that can noticeably diminish the carbon footprint of nearby river communities by harnessing kinetic energy. However, to generate ample electrical energy for end-use applications, multiple turbines must be deployed in sites hence wake recovery analysis under different operating conditions is receiving a lot of research interest. The present study numerically simulates a LHHT rotor model having an aspect ratio of 0.75 and solidity of 0.30 to investigate the performance and wake recovery distance under different tip speed ratios and flow velocities considered in the range of 0.6-1.4 and 1.0–2.0 m/sec, respectively. Moreover, an experimental study was also conducted to validate the numerical approach and found good agreement in performance results. Simulation outcomes show that a peak power coefficient of 0.17 is perceived, corresponding to a V of 1.0 m/sec; however, it drops significantly with an increase in velocity. The wake velocity deficit is found to be dissipated at a distance of 17, 15 and 15 times the rotor diameter from the centre of rotor with minima of <0.05 for V of 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 m/sec, respectively.

articleTitle: Data Cleaning and Modeling of Wind Power Curves
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The wind power curve is not only a key indicator for evaluating the performance of wind turbines, but also an important consideration for wind power system design and wind farm scheduling. However, the actual operation data contains a large amount of abnormal data, which brings serious impact on the fitting of wind power curve. In this paper, after analyzing the wind speed and power data collected by the data acquisition and monitoring (SCADA) system, we propose the mean-variance-double-ended variable-point sliding-difference method to reject the anomalous data, and use the four-parameter logistic function and the higher-order polynomial function to model wind power curves from the anomalous processed data. Then, the state of the wind turbine is evaluated by comparing the standard curves provided by the manufacturers. The results show that the method is more effective in identifying abnormal data, generalizable, and improves the accuracy of wind power curve fitting.

articleTitle: A Misalignment-Insensitive Wireless Charging System with Constant-Voltage and Constant-Current Charging Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The charging process of lithium-ion battery in wireless charging system of electric vehicle needs to go through constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) charging stages. In this paper, a new topology of reconfigurable wireless charging system based on hybrid topology is proposed to realize CC and CV outputs. The system only needs to add four relays. After opening the corresponding two relays, the system can switch between CC and CV modes respectively. In addition, the system can design its own gain in CC and CV output modes. At the same time, the magnetic coupling mechanism proposed in this paper can realize horizontal and vertical deflection, and the deflection rate reaches 83.33%. During the deflection process, the output voltage and current, the power and efficiency of the system output are relatively stable. In this paper, an experimental prototype with the highest efficiency of 94.52% is developed, and the effectiveness of the designed system can be verified from the experimental structure.

articleTitle: Self-consumption Optimization of Balcony Solar Systems Using a Load-controlled Battery Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Installing an energy storage system with a full-scale solar plant in houses is currently common practice. Doing the same for small balcony solar plants consisting only of one or two solar panels and a grid-tie inverter plugged into a standard power socket is rather uncommon. The popular belief is that this is neither necessary nor can it be economical. This paper shows that the self-consumption rate without storage is often significantly below expectations and presents an economically viable solution to greatly increase self-consumption that has already been successfully tested under real conditions for a year.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of Hydrogen Fuel Cell and Battery Freight Locomotive using EMR and Simulink
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Currently, initiatives are made to implement zerocarbon technologies and replace trains that use fossil fuels. Transportation is one of the significant sources of carbon emissions. This work investigates the applicability of fuel cell and battery technology to freight railway lines on the pit-to-port manganese line between Hotazel and Port of Ngqura in South Africa. Energetic macroscopic representation (EMR) and MATLAB/Simulink are used to control, represent and simulate interactions and power transfer of the system. The sizing of onboard sources (fuel cells and batteries) is done such that, the retrofit space constraint is respected. The results show the required traction energy peak of 89 MWh and reduced to 65 MWh due to regenerated energy. Battery charged to 74% at the end of the one-way trip. However, due to constraints on battery capacity, a substantial amount of the regenerated energy is wasted as heat. Furthermore, it was found that the size constraint sources are feasible to deliver the required payload.

articleTitle: Gaussian Mixture Models and its Parameter Estimation to Describe the Distributions of PMU Random Errors in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The distributions of PMU measurement errors are unclear, which can affect the accuracy of PMU-based applications. Therefore, PMU error analysis is an important issue in modern power systems. There are two main difficulties for PMU error analysis, which are obtaining available data to reflect the randomness of PMU errors and determining the distribution models with accurate parameters. To solve these difficulties, a method for PMU random error analysis is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a two-mode Gaussian mixture model with the reasonable selection of the number of mixture modes is proposed to describe the randomness of PMU random errors. Secondly, the differences between the samples at adjacent time sections are utilized to solve the unavailability of the true values in practical power systems. Thirdly, based on EM algorithm with additional constraints, a parameter estimation method for the two-mode Gaussian mixture model is proposed. Finally, the applicability and accuracy of the proposed method for PMU random error analysis are verified by IEEE 14 bus system.

articleTitle: A Modified Maximum Spanning Tree Based Topology Identification Method for Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The topology identification technology of distribution networks, as the foundation of distribution network state estimation, is of great significance for achieving observability, measurability, and controllability of distribution networks. This paper proposes a distribution network topology identification method based on modified maximum Spanning tree, which employs Pearson correlation coefficient as the weight to achieve accurate identification of distribution networks. The case study based on IEEE 33 bus system demonstrates the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method in topology identification.

articleTitle: An Anti-Misalignment Wireless Charging System for Low-Power Applications Based on Solenoid Coils Incorporated with Reverse Windings
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Many low-power gadgets can employ wireless charging technology, but this causes significant changes in mutual inductance while the device is in motion during charging. This paper offers a design approach that makes use of reverse windings (RWs) in order to solve this issue by maximizing average mutual inductance and stabilizing its variance. The RW extends from the planer coil to the solenoid. Through the optimization process, the degree of mutual inductance fluctuation is reduced nearly twice. The transmitter side places seven solenoids in a hexagonal package, and the receiver can cover a larger transmission area during migration. The effectiveness of the suggested design method has been validated by the experimental results.

articleTitle: Kinetic Modelling of Conventional and Renewable Jet Fuels
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In this study, the autoignition behaviors of the conventional and renewable jet fuels are investigated through chemical kinetic modelling approach using a multi-component fuel surrogate model. The composition of the surrogates was first determined based on the actual conventional jet fuel, JP-5, and renewable jet fuel, HRJ. A fuel surrogate model comprising 156 species and 514 reactions are then developed and validated to investigate the combustion characteristics and emissions performance of these fuels. The results from the validation exercise with respect to the constant volume combustion chamber and shock tube experiments showed good agreement with experimental measurements, providing confidence in the accuracy of the developed chemistry model. The sensitivity analysis indicated that H-atom abstractions on the fuels are more prevailing for all the fuel-lean conditions for both fuels. The study has also revealed the potential of HRJ in reducing both unburned hydrocarbons and soot emissions, presenting a more environmentally friendly options for the aviation industry. This research could facilitate in developing a clean, yet cost-effective SAF that is derived from renewable resources.

articleTitle: Validity Analysis of Effective State Quantities of Oil Immersed Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: With the demand of condition-based maintenance conducted in power transformers, it is crucial to select effective state quantities so as to evaluate the health status of transformers. This article comprehensively analyzes the validity of various state quantities based on historical data in transformer maintenance. According to approximately 800 abnormal events over ten years of operation and maintenance, most transformer faults are detected by inspection accounting for 71.93%, followed by oil tests and electrical tests. Putting it in detail, different detection methods of state quantities are categorized. By analyzing the validity of effective quantities, the most effective variables are sorted after, including dissolved gas analysis in oil, DC resistance, insulation resistance of iron core clamps, grounding current of iron core clamps, and short-circuit impedance. Besides, some state variables which need power outage can be equivalent to those with no need of power outage. In order to reduce the use of power outage detection, a process for obtaining the optimized quantities without power outage is proposed. The research results have reference significance for the reliability operation and maintenance of power transformers.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Core Material in Structured-core Transparent Vacuum Insulation Panels For Windows: Numerical and Experimental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The conversion of existing buildings to net zero-energy houses and net zero-energy buildings requires increased overall thermal insulation, in which the insulation of window surfaces is particularly important and effective route. The authors’ research group has proposed a form of transparent vacuum insulation panels (TVIP), which could be used as simple and easy to install insulation to building windows. In this study, several 3D-printed core types were simulated and experimentally measured to compare the effectiveness of different core architectures as well as added vacuum layers. It was found that while there were differences between frame and peak type cores, these became negligible with smaller core spans, and largely disappeared when attached to a windowpane. A second layer of vacuum improved the sample core’s overall heat transfer by 50 percent, while a third layer brought only a 24 percent improvement. Added benefits brought by the additional layers thus need to be balanced with the additional thickness inherent in the decision. It was also proven from experiments, that U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TVIP</inf> of a single frame type core with double low-E films was 1.7 [W/(m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>K)], and the U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TVIP</inf> of double vacuum layer TVIP were 1.4 [W/(m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>K)]. Higher insulation performance can thus be achieved in both ways. The created ANSYS model’s predictions followed physical test results closely, validating said model as a tool for further structured-core experiments.

Author Keywords: simultaneous vacuuming and thermal conductivity measurement

articleTitle: An Updated Microgrid Hierarchical Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Recent findings in microgrids control confirm that the current definition for hierarchical control structure (primary, secondary, and tertiary controls), which was initially inspired by the hierarchical frequency control levels in power systems is inadequate for classifying different control tasks and covering all possible control loops. This paper presents a critical review of the existing three-level control structure and proposes an updated generalized four-level hierarchical control scheme consisting of local, supplementary, central, and global controls to cover the shortcomings. The increasing deployment of microgrids in real-world power grids and the growing body of research in this field highlight the significance of this updated control framework for low/medium voltage energy networks.

articleTitle: Emission Mitigation Dispatch in Wind Power Generation with Expedited Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In this paper: a machine learning (ML) module is presented for emission mitigation dispatch (EMD) in wind power (WP) generation. It is developed for the mobile edge computing (MEC) platforms. Therefore, the module is based on a lightweight ML scheme: radial basis neural network (RBN). It has been well known that RBN is compact compared with a more popular ML scheme: feedforward neural network. However, this is the first study to combine EMD with RBN, strongly motivated by the MEC implementations. MEC is becoming an important platform in the evolving smart grid program. As a trial, a case study with 36 generators and 50 wind turbines is presented. Two standard ML stages, training and testing, are conducted in the simulation. It is shown that, by using the trained RBN, the time of solving EMD is significantly reduced. It is expected to be a desirable model for MEC.

articleTitle: Graphene-modified Phase Change Microcapsules for Thermal Storage and Electromagnetic Energy Absorption
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: As electronic devices rapidly advance towards miniaturization and integration, heat accumulation and severe electromagnetic interference inevitably occur within limited spaces, impacting the lifespan of the devices. Applying composite material as a board in electronic device applications enables electromagnetic shielding and heat absorption. In this study, melamine-urea-formaldehyde (MUF) co-condensed resin was used as the wall material, while paraffin (PA) served as the encapsulation core material to prepare MUF/PA phase change capsules. Through tests such as SEM, DSC, TGA, and infrared thermography, the MUF/PA capsule demonstrates ideal morphology, good thermal performance and excellent leak-proof capability. Subsequently, a small amount of graphene was added to the core material, forming composite phase change capsules capable of absorbing microwaves, which can improve electromagnetic interference problems. This present strategy of phase change microcapsules has great potential to apply in energy storage devices.

articleTitle: Thermohydraulic Analysis of Double Pass Solar Air Heater Duct with Perforated Blocks and Semicircular Tubes as Artificial Roughness
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Solar air heaters (SAHs) convert solar energy into thermal energy for low-temperature applications. In this study, a three-dimensional computational method is used to examine the thermohydraulic performance of double-pass solar air heater (DPSAH) having perforated blocks and semicircular tubes as roughness elements. The analysis is conducted at Reynolds numbers (Re) of 3000 to 19000, relative roughness height ratio (e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>/H) of 0.4 to 0.8, open area ratio (ϕ) of 13 to 30%, and tube amplitude ratio (a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>/H) of 0.2 to 0.5. To validate the numerical results, the experiment was conducted for the range of Re from 3000 to 15000, e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>/H of 0.4, ϕ of 30% and a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>/H of 0.3. It was found that the results of the experiment were in close agreement with those of the simulation, with a mean absolute percentage error for Nusselt number of 1.82% and friction factor of 5.28%. Based on the comparison of the thermohydraulic performance parameter (THPP) with the smooth double pass duct, the maximum THPP value is reported as 3.07. This corresponding to a value of Re as 3000, ϕ of 30%, e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</inf>/H of 0.4, and a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>/H of 0.3. In light of the research outputs presented, researchers and manufacturers can develop and design double-pass solar drying systems for various applications, including timber drying, poultry farming, solar drying, and space heating.

articleTitle: Elaboration on the Need for Dynamic Total-Cost-of- Ownership Models in the Context of Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The growing needs for alternative, sustainable powertrains are placing hydrogen mobility at the center of numerous discussions. In this context, hydrogen-powered fuel cells have high potential, especially in the commercial vehicle segment. In order to enable the transition from fossil fuels to sustainable powertrain concepts, it is necessary to decrease the Total-Cost-of-Ownership (TCO) of the vehicle and to increase the lifetime of the used fuel cells, that is reduced by degradation effects. In this paper, the static TCO of fuel cell-based commercial vehicles is compared with battery-electric, diesel- and gas-powered commercial vehicles, and significant cost drivers are derived, whereby the focus is put onto buses. Based on different driving cycles as well as degradation models, an analysis of the degradation effects that occur during the life cycle and a prediction of the expected lifetime of the fuel cell are presented. It is shown that due to the performance reducing degradation effects a dynamic approach of the TCO becomes necessary. This necessity is emphasized by further TCO parameters that will change significantly in the next few years and accordingly influence the economic viability of the considered vehicle types.

articleTitle: Permutation-based Time-Series Correlation Analysis for Customer Phase Identification from Low-Voltage Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: To prevent phase imbalance and ensure reliable distribution system operation, effective management of customer phase connectivity in a distribution network is essential. However, in many cases, obtaining accurate phase connectivity information is expensive and time-consuming as it inevitably requires either manual intervention or the use of costly advanced diagnostic tools. Considering cases where reference phase connections in three-phase power systems are unreliable, we propose a phase estimation method based on the correlation between voltage time series collected at the data central unit (DCU) and advanced metering infrastructure (AMI). In particular, our method represents phase connection estimates as permutations and efficiently finds the best phase connection configuration by considering only the important permutations. Experimental results show that the proposed method effectively identifies customer phase connections while reducing the search space by excluding insignificant permutations.

articleTitle: Influence of Load Model on Short-circuit Current Calculation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In this paper, firstly, based on the domestic and international short-circuit current calculation standards, the current situation of short-circuit current calculation on load at home and abroad is analyzed, then the conventional calculation method of short-circuit current is introduced, then the process of induction motor affecting short-circuit current in transmission network is analyzed, then the influence of variable frequency load plus motor on short-circuit current is analyzed, then the influence of electrolytic aluminum load on short-circuit current is studied, and finally the influence of comprehensive load model considering induction motor on short-circuit current is analyzed.

articleTitle: Calculation Framework of Parameters in Management of Distributed Energy Resources Considering Balance of Power Supply and Demand
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper presents a framework calculating parameters in distributed energy resource (DER) management. It is designed for retail power suppliers holding energy resource aggregator’s functions. The calculation framework includes two models of demand response (DR) programs: one is price-based DR, and the other is incentive-based one. For each DR program, the parameters are electricity prices or rebate levels. The authors formulate a power trade between the retail power suppliers and their consumers as a social welfare maximization (SWM) problem. From the viewpoint of SWM, the authors theoretically design the way to set the parameters of the DER management with maximizing the social welfare, while reducing imbalance between power supply and demand. The social welfare is defined as the sum of the retail power suppliers’ surplus and the consumers’ one in this paper. Through numerical simulations, the authors validate that the calculation framework induces the amount of power consumption to the target value of the DER management and increases the social welfare with reducing the power imbalance.

Author Keywords: imbalance between power supply and demand

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Location of Energy Storage Under the Background of Large-scale Photovoltaic Development in the Whole County
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In recent years, the problem of environmental pollution and resource depletion has become increasingly serious, and people urgently need to establish a new power system with new energy as the theme, thus, the state put forward the development strategy of large-scale distributed photovoltaic in the whole county. However, distributed photovoltaic is greatly affected by environmental and meteorological factors such as irradiance and temperature, resulting in randomness, volatility and intermittency of its output, which is bound to bring pressure on the safe and stable operation of the traditional power grid. At present, it is generally believed that the use of energy storage system to achieve energy transfer, rapid response, flexible control characteristics can greatly alleviate the pressure of distribution network. This paper establishes an energy storage optimization configuration model with node voltage fluctuation, load fluctuation and comprehensive minimum energy storage configuration capacity as optimization objectives. The solution process is based on multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm, which guides the ratio of inertia weight according to the distance between particles and the optimal particles in the population, and selects the optimal access scheme of energy storage from Pareto solution set. The effectiveness of this method is verified by simulation in IEEE-33 node distribution system, and the optimal access location of energy storage is obtained.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Dispatch of Multi-energy Complementary Traction Power Supply System Based on PV Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: To improve the stability and economy of traction power supply system, an optimal scheduling method of multi-energy complementary traction power supply system considering uncertainty was proposed. The photovoltaic and hydrogen energy are connected to the traction power supply system, which is helpful to solve the problem of abandoned light and complete the energy supply of the hydrogen energy railway project operation car. Firstly, a multi-energy complementary traction power supply system structure was constructed. The minimum daily operating cost of the system was taken as the objective function, and the system optimal scheduling model was established under the condition of power constraint. Finally, PV uncertainties are handled in a robust optimization manner. The results of the case analysis show that the optimal scheduling can obtain the output results under the economic optimal condition, and considering the uncertainty of the photovoltaic output can make the power of each module of the system more reasonable, which has a positive effect on reducing the operating cost and improving the operation reliability of the traction power supply system.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Battery Degradation Model under Different Cycling Conditions using Probabilistic NN-GA
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Predicting battery State of Health (SoH) is crucial in assessing its performance degradation to ensure safe operation and minimize the risks of failure in electric vehicle application. Different predictive models have been established as a stand-alone or optimization algorithms for model-based approach. Existing works have shown that Neural Network (NN) coupled with optimization algorithms such as Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), Genetic Algorithm (GA), etc., as well as probabilistic NN have better prediction accuracy. This study aims at exploring the potential of GA as optimization algorithm while leveraging on the statistical memory of probability distribution of the solutions in predicting the battery degradation. Two types of NN architecture were constructed where the hyper-parameters of each were (1) based on the existing work and (2) optimized by GA, known as NN-GA. Both architectures were evaluated under varying operating temperatures and multiple discharging profile. It is found that NN-GA outperforms NN under all operating temperatures with Mean Absolute Percentage (MAPE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.68%, 0.0137 and 0.01 respectively. For cold (4°C) and hot (43°C) operating temperature, NN-GA predicts the degradation with MAPE of 0.98% and 1.24%, an improvement by 0.63% and 0.74% respectively.

articleTitle: Transient Response Enhancement in an AC Microgrid Using a Simple Two-Stage Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper addresses a modified PI controller for a grid-forming converter in an islanded microgrid. The proposed control technique uses a two-stage strategy, one plus propotional-derivative with propotional-inegral ((1+PD)+PI) controller, which can reduce the effect of high-frequency noise caused by the converter switching. Simulation results for a grid-forming converter in an islanded microgrid confirm the performance and effectiveness of the proposed control method. It is shown that the proposed controller can improve transient stability much better compared to the well tuned single PI controller. Implementing this method does not increase the complexity of the system, and the performance is more superior than the conventional primary controller, which can be considered as the main benefit of this method.

articleTitle: Droop Control Method for Grid-forming Inverters Based on Virtual Inertia of Lead-lag links
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The increasing proportion of distributed generation (DG) leads to a significant decrease in the effective inertia of the power system and a weakening trend in system strength, resulting in increasingly severe stability issues. This paper presents a droop control method based on virtual inertia of lead-lag links to improve the performance of grid-forming inverters in stand-alone and grid-connected operation modes. By adding lead-lag links on the basis of traditional droop control, the zero and pole parameters of the lead-lag links are adjusted to ensure that the inverter has sufficient virtual inertia during the transient process while increasing its damping oscillation ability. It can provide virtual inertia and damping rate of change of frequency (ROCOF) in stand-alone operation mode, damp power oscillation and shorten adjustment time in grid-connected operation mode. The small signal model and simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: AC-link Voltage Harmonic Suppression Control of Cascaded MMC and Cycloconverter Based Machine Drive System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The cascaded modular multilevel converter (MMC) and cycloconverter (CCV) based machine drive system is a potential candidate for the low-speed and high-torque applications. However, the ac-link current of the drive system contains harmonics in variable frequencies, which will induce the distortion of ac-link voltage. This paper proposes an ac-link voltage harmonic suppression control of the drive system. Based on the electrical rotor angle, proposed control applies multiple synchronous rotating frames to counteract the frequency change of subharmonics in the current error. Since the subharmonics in variable frequencies are transformed into the odd and even harmonics in fixed frequencies, proposed control strategy can extract and eliminate the ac-link voltage harmonics at different machine speeds. The simulation validates the performance of control strategy.

articleTitle: Privacy preserving Double Auction using Secure Multiparty Computation for Local Electricity Markets
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: A major challenge for the implementation of local electricity markets (LEM) with small-scale prosumers is to ensure the security and privacy of data. The prosumers will need to reveal their future energy usage to the market operator (MO), which is a huge privacy concern. To address this issue, this paper presents a double auction model for local electricity markets, where the MO does not have access to the individual prosumer’s bids, ensuring complete privacy for prosumers. The scheme uses Pallier encryption cryptosystem which allows aggregation of prosumer bids without the need for decryption. The MO receives only the aggregated prosumer bids, for implementing the double auction algorithm. The proposed scheme is illustrated through a case study with 15 prosumers in a LEM.

articleTitle: Load Forecasting for Steel Enterprises Based on Prophet and Bi-LSTM Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Power load forecasting is of great significance in the production and operation activities of steel enterprises. Based on the existing Bi LSTM power load forecasting problems of gradient vanishing and explosion, this paper proposes a power load forecasting method that integrates Prophet algorithm and Bi LSTM algorithm. On the basis of the Bi-LSTM model, the Prophet algorithm is used to solve the problem of gradient vanishing and exploding in the Bi LSTM model after using the backpropagation algorithm, thereby improving the accuracy of power load forecasting. The experimental results show that using the model proposed in this article for load forecasting has higher accuracy than traditional RNN, LSTM, and Bi LSTM algorithms, verifying the effectiveness of this algorithm in improving the accuracy of load forecasting.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Charging Stations in Electric Bus Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This project proposes algorithms for optimal placement of charging infrastructure in electric bus networks. The proposed model along with the mechanisms described, has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and sustainability of bus transportation systems. The use of fast en-route charging stations and the Dynamic Battery Electric Bus Ranging mechanism can help to minimize idle time and ensure that buses are always charged enough to complete their routes. The ability to engage the entire battery electric bus network in a demand response program is also an important feature of the model, as it allows for greater flexibility and control over energy usage and grid stability. The use of graph theory to minimize fleet size and locate charging stations optimally is a powerful tool that can help to reduce costs and improve the overall effectiveness of the transportation system. The implementation of the model for Melbourne, Australia and Manchester, United Kingdom and the demonstration of significant fleet size reductions in both locations are promising results that indicate the potential for this model to be applied in other cities around the world. We show that the model can reduce the fleet size by 27.5% and 22.0% for mentioned cities respectively.

articleTitle: Comparison of Perovskite Deposition Method on Carbon-based Perovskite Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The increasing energy demand and the urge to tackle the climate crisis have assembled a global movement to shift from using fossil fuels for energy generation to clean energy sources. Perovskite solar cells are a promising candidate to fulfill future electricity demand because they can generate high efficiency while maintaining a low production cost. Although several deposition techniques may be employed to create perovskite film, solution-based deposition is the most common and extensively utilized in the fabrication of perovskite solar cells. Solution-based deposition methods can produce high-quality perovskite films using relatively simple and low-energy equipment. Furthermore, it is possible to tailor the precursor solution and deposition method to enhance the film quality. Solution-based deposition methods include the one-step and two-step methods. Each method has its advantages and disadvantages. On the other hand, the use of carbon as a counter electrode can increase the stability of the perovskite solar cell due to its hydrophobic properties. Perovskite material is well-known for its susceptibility to water, even moisture. This research investigates the use of one-step and two-step deposition methods on carbon-based perovskite solar cells. Different morphology produced from each deposition method has different effects on the interface between perovskite and carbon. The results demonstrate that, with an open-circuit voltage of 0.85 V, a short-circuit current density of 5.48 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and a fill factor of 0.32, the two-step technique yields a greater efficiency of 1.51%.

articleTitle: Low-carbon-emission-based Economic Optimization Scheme for a Smart Building with Multiple Energy Flows
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel economic optimization scheme that prioritizes low carbon emissions for smart buildings integrating multiple energy flows. The scheme addresses the inherent challenges faced by buildings as complex integrated energy systems, characterized by high carbon emissions and diverse optimization objectives of multiple energy flows. Firstly, we establish an incentive-based carbon emission trading mechanism. Subsequently, a multi-objective scheduling model for smart buildings is formulated, taking into account the carbon trading market and the intricate coupling of multiple energy flows. This model aims to minimize both operational costs and carbon emissions. To solve the formulated model, the Multi-objective Salp Swarm Algorithm (MSSA) is employed. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach are assessed through the simulation of various scheduling scenarios.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Steady-State Voltage Stability Indices for Parameter Validation Using ANFIS
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Precision and consistency in monitoring the voltage stability conditions of power system networks remain vital aspects of modern power system operation. Thus, this study presents a machine learning approach for comparative performance evaluation of some voltage stability indices (VSIs). Six essential power system parameters from the transmission line data and load flow solution at different real and reactive load levels are used as input information for implementing adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) models based on the subtractive clustering rules. The performance of the considered VSIs is evaluated using the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), the Percentage Relative Root-Mean-Square Error (RRMSEp), and the linear regression based on correlation coefficient R. The IEEE 30-bus system is used as a test, and the predictive analysis results are obtained for several simulation runs for parameter tuning and model regularity. Considering the MAPE analysis, FVSI with average MAPE = 4.7429% and maximum MAPE = 6.6574% outperformed the other VSIs; average MAPE values are 5.6165% for LMN, 12.4684% for NLSI and 14.7167% for LQP. The consistency of FVSI for precise monitoring of power system voltage stability condition, compared to the other VSIs, is verified by the RRMSEp and R analysis results.

articleTitle: Parameter Calculation Method of Motor Simulation Model Based on Factory Data
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Based on the factory data of induction motor (such as rated power, rated power factor, maximum torque multiple and rotor speed, etc.), a method for estimating the parameters of single cage model of motor suitable for electromechanical transient simulation of power system is proposed. The algorithm fully considers the physical mechanism characteristics of torque-slip of motor, and has good convergence characteristics and strong robustness. By calculating the single cage model parameters of 15 actual motors, their electromagnetic torque-slip characteristics are analyzed and compared with the factory data. The results show that the model parameters calculated according to the algorithm have high accuracy in simulating the electromechanical transient characteristics of motors, which proves the effectiveness of the algorithm. Finally, the validity and applicability of the proposed algorithm are further verified by comparing the dynamic physical simulation experiment with the numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Influence of Angle of Attack on the Performance of Solar Air Heater Having Cylindrical Jet Impingement Plate
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In the global energy transition, solar energy is among the briskly expanding renewable energy sources. In terms of solar energy utilization, solar air heater (SAH) with jet impingement is one of the promising techniques that enhances the thermo-hydraulic performance of the system covering a wide range of applications, including space heating and agricultural drying. Previous studies analyzed the performance of SAH using straight cylindrical jet; however, the influence of angle of attack still remains the research gap. Keeping in this view, the present study aims is to investigate such effect by varying angle of attack (α) in the range from 45°-75° on the thermo-hydraulic performance of SAH having cylindrical jet through numerical analysis. A 3D CFD model is developed and simulated considering mass flow rate range of 0.0104-0.0524 kg/s which altered Reynolds number (Re) from 3500-17500 while maintaining a solar radiation of 1000 W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. In order to visualize the flow physics, pressure, velocity streamlines, and turbulence kinetic energy contours are presented and discussed. The simulation results show that an α influence the thermohydraulic performance of SAH using cylindrical jet impingement significantly and is found as 2.548 at an α of 75° and Re of 17500.

articleTitle: Yogi-mLSTM Cable Partial Discharge Identification Method Based on Wavelet Threshold Denoising
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: High voltage cables are important power equipment in the power system, and their operating status affects the safety and reliability of power supply in the power grid. At present, there is no comprehensive technical means for identifying cable partial discharge defects, and there are also significant difficulties in collecting on-site data. Moreover, the existing cable partial discharge recognition methods have low accuracy, large workload, and incomplete systems. This paper proposes a Yogi-mLSTM cable partial discharge recognition method based on wavelet threshold denoising, which includes: collecting and obtaining cable partial discharge defect signals; Using wavelet threshold method to denoise the partial discharge signal and obtain the raw data of cable partial discharge; Normalize the raw data of cable partial discharge, then extract the main feature values as sample data, and split them into training and testing samples; Build a Yogi-mLSTM network model; Transfer the sample data to the Yogi-mLSTM network model for training, while determining the termination condition (number of iterations); Determine whether the model training meets the termination condition. If it does, input the data to be recognized into the trained diagnostic model, and then output the recognition results. If it does not, continue training the model. This method provides a feasible and reliable method for cable fault diagnosis, improves the intelligence level of the power station, and effectively ensures the safety and stability of cable operation.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of Thermal Performance of A New Multi-segmented Minichannel-based Radiant Ceiling Cooling Panel
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In this paper, a new multi-segmented minichannel heat exchanger based radiant ceiling panel (M-RCP) is proposed. Experiments to evaluate M-RCPs’ performance with different tilt angles were conducted. The result showed that the M-RCPs had an advantage compared to the conventional RCP from the viewpoint of cooling output per panel area and temperature difference. In addition, by providing the forced convection with fans, the cooling output from the M-RCP increased 3.6 times compared to that from the M-RCP without the forced convection. Furthermore, 3D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models of M-RCPs were produced and the CFD models were validated by comparing with the experimental results. The result of comparisons indicated that the CFD models can predict the cooling output with high accuracy.

articleTitle: A Currentless Circulating Current Suppressing Control for Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Circulating current harmonics of the modular multilevel converter (MMC) are superimposed on arm currents, increasing the RMS values of arm currents and increasing losses. It is necessary for the harmonics of circulating currents to be suppressed. Most existing methods of circulating current suppression require sensing of the arm currents, which increases sensors and sampling circuits, increases cost, and decreases the reliability. This paper proposes a currentless circulating current suppressing control through introducing proportional-resonant controller to suppress the harmonic voltages, thereby suppressing the harmonic currents, where the harmonic voltages are obtained by the calculation of duty ratio for submodules (SMs) and capacitor voltages in each phase. The proposed control can be easily executed by the Digital Signal Processor (DSP) controller without accessing the switching signals which are obtained in the Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), and it is suitable for single-phase or multiphase systems. In addition, it does not require the acquisition of arm currents. Simulation studies are implemented, the effectiveness is verified.

articleTitle: Control Scheme of ±800kV/10000MW HVDC Transmission System for Large-Scale Renewable Energy Bases in Gobi Areas
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Developing large-scale renewable energy bases is the key task in China’s 14th Five-Year Plan of modern energy systems. Aiming at transmitting large-scale wind power and photovoltaic power in the Gobi areas, two topologies suitable for ±800kV/10000MW HVDC transmission system are studied, namely wind-photovoltaic-bundled three-terminal MMC-HVDC system and heterogeneous series and parallel HVDC system with multiple DC voltage levels. Then, the voltage/power balance control between converters are analyzed in detail, and respective control strategies of multiple converters in the HVDC system are designed. Based on this, the overall control schemes of the two topologies are proposed. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed control strategies are verified using PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Desaturation Technology of Magnetic Field Energy Harvester Based on Feedback Winding Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The magnetic field energy harvester is suitable for the power source of sensors for power equipment state monitoring, with the advantages of easy installation and high power density. However, when the power line current is too high or the load is too large, the magnetic core used for energy harvesting may be driven into saturation region, resulting in the noise and heating, which affects the insulation performance of the magnetic field energy harvester and even threatens the safety of the monitored power equipment. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a desaturation method for magnetic field energy harvester based on feedback winding compensation for the core protection. Meanwhile, the impact of feedback current phase and amplitude on the energy harvesting power and magnetic field intensity are analyzed. The proposed method can reduce the waveform distortion caused by deep saturation of the magnetic core. Finally, both simulation and experiments have verified the correctness and effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Process Chains for Fuel Cell Production: A Questionnaire-based Study
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Fuel Cell electric vehicles using hydrogen as the main energy source are a promising alternative to conventionally powered vehicles on the road to locally emission-free mobility. However, there are still obstacles preventing the adaptation of Fuel Cell technology for widespread use in the transport sector. One major constraint can be traced back to the product costs of Fuel Cell stack and balance of plant. This is due, among other things, to the manufactory character of the production technology of Fuel Cell stacks. However, current market ramp-up scenarios forecast a significant increase in demand by 2030. Compared with the current state of the art of Fuel Cell production technology and associated volumes, industrialization tasks are foreseeable for the upcoming years. As a result, Fuel Cell stack manufacturers and research institutions are making parallel efforts to scale up production volumes of a partially unknown process chain. From the discrepancy between the market situation and the manufacturing maturity level, the practical deficit for the design of more adaptive process chains is concluded. Therefore, a questionnaire-based study was conducted to determine the current maturity of production technology and the prevailing process chain planning procedures. Roughly one hundred study participations were evaluated and weighted with regard to participant allocation.The results as well as an analysis of these with regard to future production planning procedures are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: A Wide Modulation Range Multiplexed MMC with Less SM and High Power Density for MVdc and HVdc Application
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Three-phase multiplexing arm modular multilevel converter (TPMA-MMC) exhibits its cost-efficient characteristics. However, the narrow operation range [0.82,1] of it, attributed to the limited energy balance angle, poses a challenge. This study introduces a new modulation principle, which obtains the arm energy balance regulation in the one-fundamental period. By doing so, the modulation range is successfully expanded to [0, 1] and realizes multiplexed arm modularization. Additionally, this principle further enables acceleration of the multiplexing arm energy balance. Comparative analysis reveals that TPMA-MMC exhibits several remarkable improvements in switch count, loss, and energy storage over the MMC. Additionally, the new topology and modulation principle also makes TPMA-MMC to operate at lower loss compared to the narrow operation principle. Lastly, we built the scale-down prototype to validate the proposed topology and modulation principle.

articleTitle: Impulse Aging Characteristics of ZnO Blocks under Multiple Strokes
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: ZnO blocks as the core component of ZnO arrester, its performance is directly related to the serviceability of the arrester. Multiple strokes as a common thundercloud discharge phenomenon, which will significantly accelerate the aging performance of the arrester. This paper investigated the impulse degradation characteristics of the electrical parameters of the arrester under multiple strokes. Firstly, the multiple strokes aging platform was built and the experiments of multiple strokes ZnO block were carried out. The DC parameters were then tested. Moreover, the degeneration variability of the DC parameters of the ZnO blocks under different multiple strokes was analyzed. Finally, the damage form of ZnO blocks under lightning strike and multiple strokes is analyzed. The research results in this paper can provide a foundation for exploring the impulse aging mechanism of ZnO blocks under multiple strokes.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Analysis of the Flexible Spiral Magnetic Field Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The magnetic field energy harvesting has become a more suitable method for powering the monitoring sensors due to its simple energy harvesting structure, high power density, and stable energy source. However, existing magnetic field energy harvester have limitations such as restricted installation size, single application scenario, and difficulty in installation or disassembly. Motivated by the above problems, this paper proposes a flexible spiral magnetic field energy harvesting (SMFH) method, which is verified by the establishment of energy harvesting models, theoretical derivation, and simulation analysis. On this basis, a comprehensive performance analysis is performed on the number of windings, load characteristics, flexibility, weight, and non-ideal resonant state. Also, the sensitivity of the flexible SMFEH to various parameter changes is deeply analyzed. Finally, the experiments have verified the feasibility of the flexible SMFEH.

articleTitle: Research on Type Identification of Typical Insulation Defects based on Fusion ELM Method
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Due to the random and accidental characteristics of partial discharge (PD) in engineering, it is difficult to identify type defects. In this paper, the partial discharge of four defect models including corona discharge model, internal discharge model, suspension discharge model and surface discharge model were designed and measured in laboratory. Then, based on experimental results, some typical parameters were obtained. Finally, a type identification method based on fusion extreme learning machine (FELM) method was propose to realize the fault type identification of cable defects. Test results indicate that the maximum value and the distribution of PD are different in these four defects for some differences existing in areas and internal electric field distortion of cable defects. Besides, due to the high verification accuracy, FELM method proposed in this paper can distinguish these four defect models well, which indicates this method can be used in identifying defect types of cable in future research.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Economy and Safety of Combustion for 1000MW Ultra-Supercritical Boiler
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Due to the large wall temperature deviation of a 1000MW ultra-supercritical combustion boiler, the temperatures of superheated steam and reheated steam were more than 10℃ lower than the design value. Pipe Explosion in high temperature superheater, high temperature reheater and low temperature superheater affected seriously the economy and safety of unit operation due to the blockage of oxide film. In order to solve the problem of wall temperature deviation, optimization adjustment tests were carried out, including thermal primary air leveling, coal fineness adjustment, secondary air throttle adjustment, exhaust air throttle adjustment and so on. After optimized combustion adjustment, the wall temperature distribution along the width of the furnace is more uniform. The maximum wall temperature deviations of the plate superheater, high temperature superheater, high temperature reheater and low temperature superheater are reduced by 52℃, 19℃, 17℃ and 29℃, respectively. After adjustment, the boiler efficiency increases by 0.98 percentage points. The economy and safety of boiler combustion have been significantly improved.

articleTitle: Partitioning of Distribution System into Virtual Microgrid considering Homogeneity
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The integration of a substantial amount of new energy sources into the power grid has introduced complex operational and management challenges for distribution networks. In order to facilitate the on-site consumption of new energy and alleviate the burden of system scheduling, the concept of virtual microgrids (VMs) has been proposed and extensively discussed. This paper presents a comprehensive VM planning framework aimed at allocating critical facilities including controllable distributed generations (CDGs) and normal open points (NOPs) for efficient VM operation. The planning objectives of the proposed framework include load importance and quantity homogeneity (LIQH), as well as power quality, which ensure planning reliability and energy efficiency. The linearization technique is conducted to convert the proposed nonlinear planning models into a Mixed-Integer Second Order Cone Programming (MISOCP) model. which can be readily solved by off-the-shelf solvers. The effectiveness of the VM planning model is verified through illustrative case studies, demonstrating its practical applicability.

articleTitle: Cost-Benefit Analysis and Feed-In Pricing Policy Recommendations for Geothermal Power Generation: A Monte Carlo Simulation Study in Taiwan
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This study presents a policy suggestion for the feed-in price of geothermal renewable electricity, considering the current policy in Taiwan. It incorporates Monte-Carlo numerical simulations to analyze the impact of various uncertainty parameters. The simulations focus on the key operational parameters of a 1 million watts (1MW) geothermal power plant and conduct sensitivity analyses of the internal rate of return (IRR) and net present value (NPV).The results show that under the current feed-in price scheme, investors would achieve better benefits by opting for the 2-stage feed-in price scenario. Sensitivity analysis reveals that a 10% increase in the feed-in price, which aligns with the willingness to pay (WTP) for renewable energy based on existing literature, leads to a substantial improvement in investor returns. Furthermore, increasing the electricity power plant operation rate by 10%, enhancing the efficiency of electricity generation by 10%, or reducing maintenance costs by 10% would yield nearly equivalent benefits to a direct 10% increase in the feed-in price.In promoting geothermal power generation, we should prioritize comprehensive incentives and promotions over feed-in price increases for better outcomes.

articleTitle: Research on Current Loop Composite Control Strategy for Stator Core Loss Test
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In order to test the loss of the stator core before the motor is manufactured, it is required that the total distortion (THD) of the current generated by the inverter output voltage applied to the tested object does not exceed the limit value. Through the analysis of the tested object, the relationship between the equivalent inductance value and the current is nonlinear, so that the harmonic content of the system is high, and the traditional control algorithm is difficult to meet the demand of the current waveform. In this paper, a composite control algorithm of PI controller and repetitive controller in parallel combined with quasi-resonant controller is proposed, based on the characteristics of the controlled object, together with a voltage type single-phase full-bridge inverter to realize the closed-loop control of the current. The structure and parameter design method of the control algorithm are given. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the composite control algorithm are proved by experiments.

articleTitle: Numerical Research and Optimization of the Radiator for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Electric Controller
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Modern unmanned aerial vehicles require decrease of the mass for its component to provide higher load capacity and operating range. Cooling system of the electronic components have significant mass and thus its decrease can be very beneficial to improvement of UAV performance. Two main methods of mass decrease was considered: implementation of higher number of smaller fins and using cylindrical shape of the fins. Smaller fins allows to increase fin efficiency to keep optimal temperature of the fin and cylindrical fins have higher surface-to-mass ratio which allows to decrease weight of the system. Fin efficiency as high as 96% was reached during analysis. Optimized model with smaller fins with higher distance between fins on the periphery and higher fins with less distance between them in center was suggested. Optimized model showed 17.4% mass decrease in comparison with prototype with same operating temperature of about 410 K.

articleTitle: Development of Partial Discharge Detection and Location System for Insulators of Overhead Distribution Lines Based on Ultrasound and Electromagnetic Wave
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low efficiency in partial discharge(PD) detection of existing technologies of insulators of overhead distribution lines, this paper conducts research on PD detection and location technology based on the combination of ultrasound and electromagnetic wave, and develops a corresponding detection system. Firstly, precise location of PD is achieved based on ultrasound and electromagnetic wave. The error between the proposed method and the traditional ultrasonic location method is compared and analyzed through simulation, verifying the superiority of the method based on ultrasound and electromagnetic wave with a maximum location error of less than 0.3m. Secondly, by using an ultrasonic concentrator, selecting suitable ultrasonic and electromagnetic sensors, and designing corresponding conditioning circuits, long-distance and high sensitivity detection of PD has been achieved. PD above 50pC can be effectively detected within a distance of 12m, and the delay estimation algorithm for PD signal has been implemented. Finally, the effectiveness of the developed PD detection system is verified through laboratory and on-site test.

articleTitle: Long-Term Optimization for Multi-Energy System of Net-zero Energy Residential Area with Seasonal Hydrogen Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: To address the seasonal mismatch between supply and demand in a net-zero residential area with multiple energy flows, this paper proposes a long-term optimization method that incorporates seasonal hydrogen storage (SHS). By leveraging the capability of hydrogen energy dispatch across seasons, the proposed method aims to minimize the comprehensive life cycle cost (CLCC) while maximizing energy self-sufficiency. A multi-modal utilization architecture is established, enabling the conversion of hydrogen to electricity and heat. The optimization model considers various cost components such as hydrogen supply chain cost, electricity trading, and carbon trading cost. The validity of the proposed approach is verified, highlighting the significance of a multimodal hydrogen energy utilization architecture and the benefits of considering seasonal trading.

articleTitle: Research on Transient Discharge Characteristics and Optimization Strategy of OLTC Change-over Selector
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: In order to limit the transient voltage between the change-over selector contacts, a tie-in resistor is connected between the middle of the regulating winding and the end of the main winding. If the value of tie-in resistor is not appropriate or the configuration is unreasonable, it will lead to discharge, gas production during polarity conversion and long-term overheating. Aiming at the above problems, this paper establishes a converter transformer simulation model, analyzes the development process of the transient discharge between the switch selector contacts during the polarity transition of the on load tap changer. The relationship between the transient voltage and the transformer structure parameter are obtained. And the variation rules of the recovery voltage and capacitive current between the contacts of the polarity transfer switch with different tie-in resistor values are analyzed. Finally, an optimization strategy for the selection and layout of the tie-in resistor is proposed to guide the more reasonable configuration of the tie-in resistor of the on load tap changer, considering the recovery voltage, capacitive current and oil tank heating between the contacts of the change-over selector.

articleTitle: Cross-regional Emergency Power Dispatch Optimization Method Considering the Coordination of Sending and Receiving Ends
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Considering the uncertainty of new energy output and the uneven distribution of resources in China, cross-regional electricity transmission is of great significance. In order to solve the problem of insufficient power supply or new energy abandonment due to the insufficient transaction electricity in spot market, we propose a cross-regional emergency power dispatch method to ensure the balance of the power system. Graph theory and DFS are applied to find all the dispatch paths. Besides, the available capacity of transmission channels, network losses, and transmission costs are considered to improve the accuracy of the model. Moreover, we could distribute the power to the more important area by taking the weight coefficients in to account. A case study on a two sending and receiving nodes power system is utilized to testify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Aggregation Topologies for All-DC Offshore Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Full DC offshore wind farms are the future development trend, but due to a lack of practical engineering experience, it is necessary to develop an economic analysis model of DC aggregating topology, along with a reliable large-capacity wind farm example and a comparison of various aggregating topologies. In order to improve the reliability calculation method and account for the effects of faults at various locations on the full wind farm, this paper establishes an economic analysis model from three perspectives of economy, power loss, and reliability. It also performs a quantitative comparative analysis of the calculation examples. The analysis's findings indicate that the parallel-type wind farm has higher reliability, but the series-parallel wind farm has clear advantages in terms of cost and power loss, and it is fiercely competitive when choosing the future all-DC offshore wind farm aggregation topology.

articleTitle: Optimization of EV Scheduling in a Microgrid Integrated with a Rooftop Solar System Using Forward Dynamic Programming
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) have been a trend in terms of transportation for a decade because of the energy transition. However, as the number of EVs increases, various problems related to the power quality, such as voltage and load profile, arise. To reduce the negative impact of EV charging, several solutions are suggested, with the integration of renewable energy sources into the charging station combined with Vehicle-to-Grid technology. This paper presents an algorithm to minimize the charging cost of all EVs and flatten the load curve, considering the travel schedule of EV owners and voltage constraints in the power grid.

articleTitle: Three-phase Three-level Converter and Its Control Strategy for Grid-connected High-capacity Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: When compared to AC pooling, the use of DC pooling in offshore wind farms can greatly increase transmission efficiency while lowering the cost required to build and run the wind farms. Studying the topology of the main component of the DC convergence DC/DC converter and choosing the best modulation and control strategy are particularly crucial. In this study, a three-phase, three-level DC/DC converter is chosen as the research object. A phase-shifted pulse width modulation (PSPWM) strategy is suggested, and a voltage-current double-closed-loop PI control strategy is adopted to ensure the input voltage's stability. The parameters of this converter are also corrected and optimized. The converter has both fault isolation functions and is appropriate for grid-connected situations involving a lot of power. It also has a substantial suppressive effect on the phenomenon of huge input voltage variations in offshore wind farms, which makes it possible to operate at high voltage gains. The success of the topology and control method is then confirmed using a simulation model created in Simulink and a real-time simulation platform.

articleTitle: Co-frequency Regional Power System Partition Method Based on Measured Frequency Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: To provide a theoretical foundation for dynamic equivalent analysis and partition control in frequency issues of modern power systems, we proposed a co-frequency region partition method based on measured frequency dynamics. First, define the co-frequency region according to the application requirements of frequency dynamic analysis and control. The quantitative co-frequency index of the measured frequency dynamics between buses is proposed with the correlation coefficient. Then, we propose a co-frequency region partition method based on spectral clustering algorithm. The method based on the constructed frequency dynamics similarity graph can effectively extract the information of measured data to realize an appreciate number of clusters for the power system without knowing the system models and parameters. The IEEE 118-bus test system is applied to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Finally, the application scenarios of the co-frequency region partition are further illustrated.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Location of On-Route Fast-Charging Stations in a Battery Electric Bus System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The transportation system is responsible for producing approximately 18% of total gas emissions in Australia. Electrified public transport, mainly in the form of Battery electric buses (BEBs), stands at the intersection of mobility and electricity systems and is a promising alternative for conventional bus fleets in achieving zero-emission targets. To provide reliable mobility service using BEBs, different charging methods, including battery swapping, fast and normal charging in depots, and main or on-route bus stops, are required to merge charging requirements into the bus schedule. The mobility-desired fast charging could merge BEBs into the bus network with minimum effect on bus schedules; however, it may lead to unmanageable electricity demand. Therefore, a trade-off between mobility requirements and power system constraints should be achieved in the charging process. In this research, the optimal deployment of fast-charging stations for BEBs is addressed to minimize a cost function including the total cost of vehicle batteries, number of fast-charging stations, station electrification cost, and electricity demand. It is formulated as a constrained optimization problem and is solved using mixed-integer linear programming. Numerical simulations show the efficiency of the suggested approach when applied to a real-world bus network for the eastern suburbs of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia.

articleTitle: Impedance-Based Stability Analysis of Power Systems Incorporating Inverter-Based Resources: Techniques, Methods, and Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Analysis and control methods utilizing the impedance of power sources and loads have garnered attention for enhancing the fault tolerance of power systems. However, conducting actual impedance measurements across a wide bandwidth in the laboratory poses several challenges, including the accuracy of measured values and magnetic saturation of power transformers. Therefore, this study implements a microgrid (MG) in the laboratory, consisting of a power electronics converter controlled as a virtual synchronous machine (VSM) and a power emulator, to analyze the stability of the MG by measuring the actual impedances of the converter and the grid. Various MG conditions were simulated by changing the output of the power emulator and the control of the VSM, and the required perturbation amplitude and frequency bandwidth for impedance measurements were quantitatively determined, successfully establishing an analysis method.

articleTitle: Impedance-based Voltage Stability Assessment for Grid-forming Typed VSG Inverters Connected via Distributed Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Distributed power supplies with grid stabilization functions are actively connected to the power system. Recently, many studies have been conducted on control topologies that enhance the grid stabilization effect through virtual inertia characteristics in order to achieve both transient stability of the power supply and steady-state stability of the entire system. However, these previous studies have focused on active power supply/demand and frequency stability, and few detailed studies have been conducted on reactive power transfer and voltage maintenance functions of distributed power supplies. Therefore, in this paper, first the power supplies consisting of a synchronous generator (SG) and a group of grid-forming inverters (GFMs) controlled by a virtual synchronous generator (VSG) are connected via a transmission line consisting of frequency-dependent distributed circuit to clarify the effect of inverter voltage regulation according to the SG's effective power output limit. Furthermore, the destabilizing grid operating conditions estimated from the above results were proved by impedance-based analysis, and the possibility of avoiding them by tuning the VSG control parameters was presented.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Hosting Capacity for Distribution Network Using Statistical Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) hosting capacity, which refers to the maximum amount of PV that can be stably integrated into the grid, is important to consider when integrating PV systems into the grid due to the ability of violations to the network such as overloading and voltage fluctuations. In the literature, various analysis methods were proposed to estimate the penetration of PV, which is proper to install into the distribution networks without negative impacts. This paper presents a statistical approach to calculate the hosting capacity of solar power plants in a practical 35kV distribution network in Vietnam. The uncertainties of PV production and power consumption are also considered to determine the probability of risks to the grid. The results of this study show the maximum PV hosting capacity for the distribution network under consideration and the impact of its integration on the voltage profile in the distribution network. This study highlights the difference between summer and winter scenarios in estimating the PV hosting capacity. The paper also considers the geographical conditions to determine which locations are suitable for future PV installations.

articleTitle: The Impact of Large-scale Photovoltaic Penetration on Voltage in Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Large-scale distributed PV access changes the distribution of currents in the distribution grid, and the random volatility of its output is the main cause of voltage fluctuation. In order to comprehensively reveal the impact of large-scale distributed photovoltaic penetration on voltage in distribution network, this paper analyzes the theoretical mechanism of PV access to the distribution network on voltage deviation and voltage fluctuation, building a simulation model of the distribution network and PV based on Matlab/simulink, and analyzing the impact of various factors such as grid-connected location, access mode, PV output correlation, and weather conditions on voltage. In addition, for the voltage fluctuations under different weather conditions, the envelopes of the instantaneous values of nodal voltages are extracted by finding the wave crests and cubic spline interpolation, using the Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT) method, and the envelope signals are processed by empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and the Hilbert transform, to realize a detailed analysis of the modulation signals of the voltage fluctuations.
