The results show that large-scale distributed PV access significantly increases the voltage level of distribution network, and PV using single-phase grid-connected access will cause a large effect on the node voltage three-phase unbalance. The magnitude of voltage fluctuations increases with increasing PV output correlation. Distribution network node voltage with PV output changes occur random fluctuations, node voltage amplitude modulation effect by multiple low-frequency signals, the more drastic the change in illumination radiance, the greater the change in the amplitude of the modulating wave, the larger the voltage fluctuation.

articleTitle: Development of an Energy Monitoring System with Forecasting for Off-Grid Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The need for energy, especially energy from renewable sources, to be distributed and flexible has driven the development of microgrids in recent years. They have been a key technology in achieving the sustainable development goal for energy particularly in rural off-grid areas. However, safe and reliable operation of microgrids remains a challenge given the difficulty in maintaining the physical system due to the lack of technical know-how in the rural localities where they are installed. A monitoring system with power forecasting capability is proposed in this article to aid in the safe and reliable operation of microgrids. The monitoring system features galvanic isolation in both the ac and dc measurement modules protecting users and the monitoring system itself from the high currents of the microgrid power system. The measurements can then be fed into a machine learning algorithm to forecast the power output of the microgrid. Experimental data were presented to validate the measurements and forecasts of the monitoring system. Users can monitor and forecast the power output of a microgrid and conduct maintenance if significant deviations are observed between forecasts and measurements.

articleTitle: Enhancing Building Energy Efficiency Through Its Windows
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of enhancing the energy efficiency of buildings which eventually contributes to the carbon neutrality and sustainability. To achieve that, two strategies are proposed based on the exploitation of the functioning of building windows for thermal losses prevention and renewable power generation. More specifically, the first strategy proposes an integrated control scheme for lighting and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems under controllable blinds or curtains. Numerical simulations and calculations are then carried out to show the effectiveness of this strategy. Next, in the second strategy, it is proposed to employ the so-called solar windows to obtain clean power generation via solar cells attached to building windows. A realistic experiment is performed for an office building, which reveals the viability of such solar power generation strategy.

articleTitle: Study on the Effect of Large Temperature Difference on the Aging Performance of Silicone Rubber Materials
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The altitude of ultra-high voltage transmission in China has exceeded 5000m, and the impact of extreme high-altitude environments on the insulation performance of composite insulators is gradually exposed. In high-altitude environments, due to the thin air and less weakening of light intensity, there is often an extreme climate characteristic of large temperature difference between day and night. In order to clarify the trend evolution of composite insulator silicone rubber (SiR) materials in high-altitude and large temperature difference environments, this article conducted high and low temperature alternating aging tests on silicone rubber samples at -20 ℃ to 150 ℃. The degradation law of high and low temperature alternating on silicone rubber performance was analyzed through changes in tensile strength, elongation at break, and cross-linking density, The failure mechanism of SiR was studied by scanning electron microscope (SEM), X ray diffraction analysis (XRD), fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) and thermogravimetric analysis (TG). The results indicate that under alternating high and low temperature environments, the side chains of silicone rubber molecules undergo oxidation and thermal degradation reactions, resulting in an increase in crosslinking density; The combined action of water molecules and heat causes hydrolysis reactions of chemical groups; Silicone rubber materials such as hydrated alumina and silica fillers will migrate from the body to the surface, and the precipitated Aluminium hydroxide (ATH) will undergo oxidation reactions to generate thermally stable alumina and other products, resulting in a decrease in mechanical properties, heat and cold resistance, organic group damage, and an increase in inorganic components. This provides theoretical support and practical application value for the analysis of aging failure mechanism of composite insulators in service in large temperature difference environments.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Charging Costs for Various Types of EVs in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The growing popularity of electric vehicles (EVs) has increased the demand for electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) in power distribution systems. Numerous benefits can be obtained from integrating EVCS with the optimum charging power of various EVs, such as cost-effectiveness and time reduction. Therefore, this research aims to evaluate the charging cost and charging time for various types of EVs in Malaysia. In this paper, the charging cost and charging time for different EVs in Malaysia are compared and evaluated by considering the constant charging rate of the Battery Management System (BMS) relative to the battery’s capacity. The results highlight the significance of contemplating pricing structures and charging time reductions when selecting a charging provider. The evaluation provides valuable insights into the charging costs of EVs, thereby facilitating the identification of potential user bases and the estimation of charging needs for EVs in Malaysia.

articleTitle: Research on Key Technologies of High-power IGBT Driver Integrating Real-time Monitoring and Active Control of IGBT Status
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: Insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT), as a fully controlled power electronic device, is widely used in High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) flexible equipment, and its fault modes include IGBT collector emitter over-voltage, IGBT gate emitter over-voltage, IGBT chip over-current, overheating or beyond safe operating area(SOA). Because the existing IGBT drivers only report overcurrent and undervoltage protection faults after an overcurrent or undervoltage fault occurs, and lack of real-time process monitoring of IGBT collector emitter voltage(Vce), gate emitter voltage(Vge), and other state variables, so the real fault cause and aging trend of IGBT cannot be accurately known. Based on this, This paper firstly presented the overall design scheme of the high-power IGBT driver integrating real-time monitoring and active control functions; The next chapter indicated the integrated measurement method for the IGBT collector emitter and gate emitter off-state and on-state voltage to meet the high dynamic and high precision performance of the switching transient V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ce</inf> and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ge</inf>; In the final chapter, based on practical application requirements, the experimental verification is carried out under various conditions to achieve relatively complete real-time monitoring and active control of the IGBT module, and the IGBT fault analysis and prediction model will be further established based on the measurement results.

Author Keywords: collector emitter voltage and gate emitter voltage

articleTitle: Inter-turn Fault Diagnosis for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on High Frequency Rotating Voltage Injection
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Power and Energy Systems Engineering (CPESE)
abstract: The degradation of insulation between adjacent coils of the stator winding of a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) can lead to inter-turn short-circuit faults, which will cause more serious faults if they are not detected. Therefore, in order to improve the reliability of PMSM, this paper proposes an inter-turn fault (ITF) online diagnosis method, which evaluates the ITF of a motor by injecting a high-frequency rotating voltage of fixed frequency, analyzing the current response generated by this voltage and the high-frequency voltage in the control loop, and assessing the ITF of the motor by the asymmetry of the high-frequency component of the modulated wave. Experimental results show that since the injection of high frequency rotating voltage is not affected by the current fundamental asymmetry, our proposed method is capable of diagnosing mild ITF, and the fault indicator is insensitive to sudden changes in speed and current, thus improving the robustness of fault diagnosis.
